q: Which statement best describes business analysis?
options: Managing the project schedule and budget
Determining problems and opportunities, recommending solutions, and eliciting and managing requirements
Writing the code for a software solution
explanation: Business analysis is the application of knowledge, skills, tools and techniques to determine problems and opportunities, identify business needs and recommend solutions, elicit, analyze and manage requirements, and define how value will be measured.

q: What is the fundamental difference between the business analyst and the project manager?
options: The business analyst is responsible for the product; the project manager is responsible for the project
The business analyst manages the budget; the project manager manages the scope
The business analyst reports to the project manager in every organization
The business analyst works only on IT projects
explanation: Project managers are responsible for the successful delivery of the project, while business analysts are responsible for the successful delivery of the product. The product focus is broader than the project focus.

q: A retailer's leadership sets a target for the coming year: "Increase online sales by 15%." The business analyst must classify it before any solution is discussed. Which type of requirement is it?
explanation: A business requirement describes the higher-level needs of the organization: the reason the initiative is undertaken and measurable goals the business is seeking to achieve.

q: "The system must confirm a payment within 3 seconds" is which type of requirement?
explanation: A nonfunctional requirement describes the conditions or qualities needed for the product to be effective, such as performance, reliability, security and safety. A functional requirement describes what the product does.

q: A bank is replacing its customer system. Before go-live, the existing customer records must be converted and the support staff trained. These needs disappear once the change is complete. What are they?
explanation: Transition requirements describe temporary capabilities, such as data conversion and training, needed to move from the current state to the future state. They are no longer needed once the transition is complete.

q: Which of these is a project requirement, and so is NOT part of the business analysis effort?
options: Customers want to pay quickly, without first having to create an account
The first release must be delivered by 30 June under the contract
The system is available 99.9% of the time
explanation: Project requirements describe the actions, processes or conditions the project needs to meet, such as milestone dates and contractual obligations. They are part of the project management effort, not product requirements.

q: How does a nonfunctional requirement differ from a quality requirement?
options: They are two names for the same thing
A nonfunctional requirement concerns the quality of the product; a quality requirement concerns validating project deliverables
A nonfunctional requirement is temporary; a quality requirement is permanent
A nonfunctional requirement is written by the project manager
explanation: Business analysis ensures the product is of sufficient quality through nonfunctional requirements. Project management ensures the processes and deliverables are of sufficient quality through quality requirements, such as tests and certifications.

q: How do the product life cycle and the project life cycle relate?
options: A single project life cycle contains several whole product life cycles
A product life cycle ends when the first project closes
A product life cycle may contain one or more project life cycles
explanation: A product life cycle runs from concept to retirement and may consist of multiple project life cycles. Business analysis focuses on the entire product life cycle, including the projects that advance the product.

q: Customer complaints at a company have doubled this year, but nobody has proposed a project yet. An executive asks when business analysis should start. What is the answer?
options: Before the project, with understanding the problem or opportunity
When the project charter has been signed and the team is being formed
When the project team is assigned
explanation: Business analysis begins with defining the situation and fully understanding the problem or opportunity the organization wishes to address. This work is considered pre-project.

q: Which business analysis process group investigates whether a new or changed product is viable and aligns it with strategy?
explanation: The Defining and Aligning Process Group investigates and evaluates the viability of initiating a new product or changing or retiring an existing one, and aligns products, portfolios, programs and projects to organizational strategy.

q: Which is the last of the six business analysis process groups?
explanation: The six groups are Defining and Aligning, Initiating, Planning, Executing, Monitoring and Controlling, and Releasing. Releasing decides whether a solution should be released and obtains acceptance.

q: Which statement about business analysis process groups is correct?
options: They are the phases of the project life cycle, performed one after the other in order
They are not phases; their processes can be repeated and no sequence is prescribed
They apply only to predictive projects
explanation: Process groups are not project life cycle phases. Sequence and timing are not prescribed, and processes can be repeated throughout the life cycle, for example elicitation in every iteration.

q: Which knowledge area is used throughout all business analysis work and interacts with all the others?
explanation: The processes in the Stakeholder Engagement knowledge area are used throughout all business analysis efforts and interact with all the other knowledge areas.

q: Which knowledge area validates a solution to determine how well it meets the business need and delivers value?
explanation: Solution Evaluation validates a full solution or a segment of one, about to be or already implemented, to determine how well it meets the business needs and delivers value.

q: How is business value defined?
options: The total cost of the project
The net quantifiable benefit derived from a business endeavor, tangible or intangible
The revenue in the first month after release
explanation: Business value is the net quantifiable benefit derived from a business endeavor. The benefit may be tangible, intangible or both.

q: A project's benefit, higher revenue, can only be measured a year after release. What should the team do?
options: Declare the project successful when it closes
Delay closing the project for a year
Define the objective and its measure before the project starts, take a baseline, and use a leading indicator such as customer satisfaction
explanation: Benefits are often realized well after project completion. By setting the business objective and how it will be measured before the project starts, the team can build measurement in, take a baseline, and use leading indicators such as customer satisfaction.

q: On a product team, the developers want to drop a feature, the analyst has documented it, and the project manager is worried about the date. Who has the authority to decide whether it stays in the product?
explanation: A product owner is an individual with decision-making authority for prioritizing what to include or exclude from one or more specific products. The business analyst advises and often helps refine the backlog.
ref: PMI Guide to Business Analysis, Glossary (Product Owner)

q: An agile team has a scrum master, a product owner and developers, but nobody with the title business analyst. What does this mean for business analysis?
options: No business analysis is needed on agile projects
The scrum master must do all of it
The work is still done, shared across the roles on the team
The project cannot start until a dedicated business analyst is hired
explanation: When a life cycle does not recognize the business analyst role, the work of business analysis is not overlooked. On agile projects the responsibilities may be spread across roles and depend on the needs of the team.

q: A business analyst must get agreement from several department heads who do not report to them. What does the analyst rely on?
options: Trust and influence built through honesty, integrity and transparency
The authority to schedule their work
Escalating every disagreement to the project sponsor for a binding decision
explanation: Business analysts lead and influence stakeholders without having the supervisory authority, title or rank to do so. They strengthen their leadership by building trust and showing honesty, integrity and transparency.

q: Three business analysts work on a project. Two are overloaded and the third has time to spare. Who is responsible for allocating, scheduling and tracking their work?
explanation: Business analysts may lead, but they do not oversee project resources. At the project level the project manager is responsible for resource allocation, scheduling and work progress, including that of business analysts.

q: During planning, a stakeholder group that will use the new system is overlooked. What is the most likely consequence?
explanation: Keeping the stakeholder register accurate is critical because when stakeholders are overlooked, there is a high chance that requirements will be missed.

q: A sponsor complains that two weeks of business analysis are "delaying the real work". Why does taking that time usually save time overall?
options: It removes the need for testing
Well-understood requirements reduce rework, change requests and defects later
It shortens the product life cycle
It transfers risk to the customer
explanation: Skipping business analysis leads to poorly understood requirements, missed expectations, rework and change requests. Taking the time to do it saves time, reduces cost and lowers risk exposure in the long run.

q: A sponsor asks the business analyst to move two developers onto requirements work to speed it up. What should the analyst do?
options: Reassign them at once, since requirements work is the analyst's own area
Raise the request with the project manager, who allocates resources
Ask the two developers to decide between themselves
Refuse, because requirements work cannot be sped up
explanation: Business analysts may lead, but they do not oversee project resources. At the project level the project manager is responsible for resource allocation, scheduling and work progress.
